title: All Protestants condemn the view that every precept can be kept without grace
source_text: XLVIII. Verum nullus est apud Protestantes qui non damnet quod quidam in Schola Romana docuerunt, omnia, nempe, & singula legis moralis praecepta, quoad operis substantiam, sive materiam, posse sine Christi gratia servari. Ab hoc enim numero eximunt Protestantes, ut supra vidimus, praecepta quaedam quae spectant actus animi internos, quale est praeceptum de non concupiscendo, & de Deo supra omnia diligendo.
pass_a_gloss: XLVIII. But there is none among the Protestants who does not condemn what certain in the Roman School have taught, that all, namely, and each precept of the moral law, as to the substance of the work, or matter, can without Christ's grace be kept. For from this number the Protestants except, as we saw above, certain precepts which regard internal acts of the mind, such as is the precept of not coveting, and of loving God above all things.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVIII. But there is no Protestant who does not condemn what some in the Roman School have taught: that each and every precept of the moral law can be kept without the grace of Christ as to the substance, or matter, of the work.
For, as we saw above, the Protestants except from this certain precepts that concern inward acts of the mind, such as the precept not to covet and the precept to love God above all things.
